## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Lièzǐ* — comprehensively treated at [KR5c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0049) — is one of the four Táng-canonised Daoist classics, along with the *Dàodé jīng*, *Zhuāngzǐ*, and *Kàngcāng zǐ*. The 8-*piān* structure is canonical:

1. **天瑞** (*Tiān ruì* — Auspice of Heaven)
2. **黃帝** (*Huángdì* — The Yellow Emperor)
3. **周穆王** (*Zhōu Mù wáng* — King Mù of Zhōu)
4. **仲尼** (*Zhòng Ní* — Confucius)
5. **湯問** (*Tāng wèn* — Questions of Tāng)
6. **力命** (*Lì mìng* — Power and Fate)
7. **楊朱** (*Yáng Zhū*)
8. **說符** (*Shuō fú* — Explanations of Resonances)

The received text is — per A. C. Graham's foundational philological analysis — a c. 300–370 CE Eastern-Jìn forgery composed in the immediate circle of Zhāng Zhàn 張湛 (fl. 370). See [KR5c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0049) for the full account of the text's provenance, contents, and philosophical themes.

**Abstract**

See [KR5c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0049) for the full treatment of the *Lièzǐ*'s authorship, dating, philosophical content, canonisation in 742, and modern scholarship. This [KR5c0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0124) entry is a parallel text-witness derived from an independent source tradition (CHANT / TLS rather than the Daozang).

**Dating.** Per [KR5c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0049): Eastern-Jìn 東晉 c. 300–370 CE for the received recension. Traditional attribution is to Liè Yùkòu (Warring States). The frontmatter gives **300–370** as the composition window. Dynasty: 東晉.
